subject: Issue with the survey
body:
Dear Sheri,

I apologize again for the inconvenience.

We have identified the issue, and a new version of the iOS app will be released by the end of tomorrow. In the meantime, I noticed that you've created single-choice questions with empty answer options. This is generally not advisable, as participants may select the blank option, which could complicate data analysis on your end.

To temporarily resolve the iOS issue before the new version is released, please remove any empty answer choices and republish the survey. Once the new version is available, kindly ensure that participants install the latest version. Afterward, you can revert to the original survey setup if you prefer.

Best regards,
Omid

Thanks for your email.
 
We are trying to set up a survey that allows people room to choose an item between 1 and 7. In traditional psychological formats, it is common to only provide anchors for the 1 , 4, and 7. Is there no way to accomplish that type of survey response format? We are explicitly banned from using sliders by Wellcome Trust, as the group we are working with found that those reduced variability. All tips are welcome here.

subject: Issue with the survey
body:
Dear Sheri,

I wanted to take this question. I guess that is the reason you had responses with empty content, right? You can of course use Single Answer question (radio button) for this purpose. We did not expect empty content for any of the choices in a single-answer question, and thats why the iOS app would crash. My colleague, Omid, made a change to make sure this is supported. So you can have the design you are looking for, i.e. a single-answer question with anchors only on 1, 4 and 7.

Let me know if I misunderstood anything.

Thanks,
Mohammad
